subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or reject the tool call?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but warning-only versus fail-closed changes how a denied sandbox execution capability is surfaced to users.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior, which is the narrowest compatibility-preserving fix.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose another host or execution mode before interactive tools run.

options.title: Adopt A Warning PR After Proof
options.body: Use an existing warning-PR shape only after maintainers choose the semantics and require current-main proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior, which is the narrowest compatibility-preserving fix.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across exec PTY support, fallback behavior, docs, and recent routing changes.
